## Summary

`catalyst env shell` named its writable home volume from the image digest alone, so every repository using the same image mounted the same `/home/catalyst`. Code run in repository A could leave a `.bash_profile` that ran when repository B's shell opened, with B's checkout and declared secrets available.

Each checkout now gets its own home volume, named `catalyst-env-home-<12 hex of image digest>-<24 hex>`. The last part is the first 24 hex characters of a sha256 over the checkout's real path, the inode and birth time of the root directory, and the inode and birth time of the root's own `.git` entry (read with `lstat`). When the root or its `.git` has no birth time, or there is no `.git`, the run gets an anonymous home volume that `--rm` removes with the container, so no other run can mount it.

## Ticket requirements

- **Scope the volume per repository.** Met. `homeVolumeFor(image, root, identity)` (`src/env/shell-plan.ts:52`) builds the name above. Its only caller (`src/env/shell-plan.ts:120`) passes `input.root`, the host path mounted at `/workspace`, and `input.rootIdentity`, which `runEnvShell` fills from `checkoutIdentity(root)` (`src/env/shell.ts:264`). Nothing inside the container can set a directory's inode or birth time, so code in the container cannot choose its own volume. The name does not use the origin URL or the git common dir, because files in the checkout decide those. `shell` and `--check` in one checkout share a volume, so toolchains and history persist per repository, and a new image starts fresh.
- **Acceptance: a test that fails on a1126ea9 and passes with the fix.** Met. Two tests compare the volume mount of two checkouts on one image: `test/env-shell-plan.test.ts:41` on the argv builder, and `test/env-shell.test.ts:541` through `main`, with the same origin name and git common dir for both checkouts. Validation ran both against `a1126ea9` (fetched through `refs/pull/407/head`), and both failed because the two repositories got the identical image-only volume word. Both pass at this head.

## Why the key grew beyond the path

The first version keyed on the path alone. Four review findings, from a model of another family, showed that a path names a place and not a repository. All four are fixed, and each fix has a test that failed before it.

- A repository deleted and a different one cloned at the same path inherited the old volume. The key now includes the root's inode and birth time.
- The first version of that fix fell back to the inode when the birth time equalled the change time. On a coarse-timestamp filesystem a new root has equal times, so adding a file to the root changed the name. The change time is never read now.
- With no birth time at all, a reused inode could repeat a name. That case now gets an anonymous home volume.
- Emptying the root and putting another repository's contents and `.git` inside it kept the root's inode and birth time. The key now also includes the inode and birth time of the root's own `.git` entry. Replacing a repository in place creates a new `.git`, so the volume changes. A `.git` symlink planted from the container has its own identity and is never followed.

## Changes Made

- `src/env/shell-plan.ts`: `homeVolumeFor` takes the root and an identity string and returns a 55-character name. `ShellRunInput` gains `rootIdentity: string | null`. When it is null, `shellRunArgs` mounts `type=volume,dst=/home/catalyst` with no source. The header comment is updated.
- `src/env/shell.ts`: new `identityFromStat` (pure) and `checkoutIdentity` (reads the stat of the root and `lstat` of `.git`, with no git call), called when the run input is built. The code comment there states the accepted limits below.
- `test/env-shell-plan.test.ts`: the pinned volume names are updated. New tests cover two repositories getting different volumes, one repository keeping its volume across shell, non-terminal and `--check` modes, the identity key, no named volume when `rootIdentity` is null, and the name format for odd roots (spaces, non-ASCII, 400 characters, Windows-style paths).
- `test/env-shell.test.ts`: through-`main` tests for two checkouts with the same origin, a directory deleted and re-created at the same path, replacement in place, a planted `.git` symlink, a checkout with no `.git`, and a stable name while root entries and `.git` contents change.
- `thoughts/shared/`: research, plan, validation and this description.

## Accepted limits

These are stated in the comments in `src/env/shell.ts`.

- A person who keeps A's `.git` and repoints it at B (set-url, fetch, checkout) still has A's repository as far as git can tell. A's hooks and config persist in that `.git` anyway, so the home volume adds nothing, and the key stays free of the origin URL and other checkout-writable data.
- Anonymous home volumes (no birth time, or no `.git`, such as a non-git `--root`) lose toolchains and history when the container exits, so toolchains download again on every run there. This is the cost of never sharing a home across repositories.
- Some worktree operations rewrite the `.git` file. That rotates the volume and never shares one.
- Where Node synthesizes the birth time from the change time (no statx, for example blocked by a sandbox; not on Node 24's supported kernels), the name changes when entries at the root change. That checkout gets a fresh volume and never shares one. The reviewer accepted this as a follow-up.
- Moving or restoring a checkout starts a fresh home. Old shared volumes (`catalyst-env-home-<12 hex>`) stay on disk, unmounted.
- The git common dir mount is chosen by files in the checkout. The plan leaves it to a separate ticket.

## How to Verify It

- [x] ✅ Typecheck passes: `npm run typecheck`
- [x] ✅ Env shell tests pass (60 of 60): `npx vitest run test/env-shell-plan.test.ts test/env-shell.test.ts`
- [x] ✅ CI checks on this PR pass (CodeQL, analysis, skill routing evals, bun-runtime, check); Mergify merge checks are skipped
- [ ] Not run: the Docker anonymous-volume behaviour. This container has no Docker. Docker documents that a new anonymous volume is populated from the image's `/home/catalyst` content, as a named one is, and `--rm` removes it with the container. Please confirm with Docker: run `catalyst env shell` in a directory with no `.git`, exit, and check that `docker volume ls` shows no new volume.
- [ ] Manual, with Docker: run `catalyst env shell` in two checkouts, then `docker volume ls --filter name=catalyst-env-home-`. Expect two distinct 55-character names, and `--check` reusing the first.
- [ ] Manual: append `echo PWNED >> ~/.bashrc` in checkout A's shell, then open B's shell on a terminal. `PWNED` must not print.

## Changelog Entry

Fixed: `catalyst env shell` keeps one home volume for each repository checkout, so a shell in one repository can no longer plant startup files that run in another, even when a different repository is later put at the same path.
